name: VSA 9 configuration audit and cross-RMM mapper
demand: There is a verified deadline: Kaseya says VSA 9 will be decommissioned on 2027-08-31 and directs customers to Datto RMM or VSA 10 (https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb/articles/49926799653265-VSA-9-End-of-Life-Notice). Kaseya reported more than 40,000 MSP and SMB customers globally in 2026, but that figure covers its whole customer base, not VSA 9 users (https://www.kaseya.com/press-release/ai-emerges-as-the-key-to-scaling-msp-operations-as-growth-gets-harder/). VSA 9 customer count, active installs, independent-switcher count, and current search volume are unverified. Google Keyword Planner can report searches by location and date range, but I did not retrieve a volume figure (https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7337243?hl=en).
prices: NinjaOne publishes a range of $1.50 per endpoint/month at 10,000 endpoints to $3.75 at 50 or fewer, with regional and product variation (https://www.ninjaone.com/msp/pricing/). Datto RMM and N-able N-central require quote requests (https://www.datto.com/request/rmm-pricing/; https://www.n-able.com/products/n-central-rmm/quote). ProVal's VSA 9-to-Datto migration page does not publish a price; its price is unverified (https://content.provaltech.com/docs/38446fc5-ce0a-4319-9471-ce7e327d8a8d/).
copy_speed: A close adjacent launch is verified: ProVal published a VSA 9-to-Datto migration solution on 2026-10-16. It creates sites, installs agents, and reports missing devices; the described scope does not cover cross-vendor policy or script conversion (https://content.provaltech.com/docs/38446fc5-ce0a-4319-9471-ce7e327d8a8d/). I found no independent cross-RMM mapper launch in the searches reviewed; that is not proof none exists.
platform_risk: High. Kaseya's stated migration destinations are Datto RMM and VSA 10, and ProVal's recent tool targets Datto (https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb/articles/49926799653265-VSA-9-End-of-Life-Notice; https://content.provaltech.com/docs/38446fc5-ce0a-4319-9471-ce7e327d8a8d/). VSA's Import Center exports automation objects in VSA XML, including procedures, monitor sets, patch policies, and policies (https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007940918-What-can-I-migrate-from-On-Premise-to-SaaS-or-SaaS-to-On-Premise). NinjaOne's public API documents policy creation and condition operations, while its scripts endpoint is documented as listing scripts; its documentation describes UI-based script import (https://app.ninjaone.com/apidocs-beta/core-resources/operations/createPolicy; https://app.ninjaone.com/apidocs-beta/core-resources/operations/getAutomationScripts; https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/endpoint-management/scripting-and-automation/getting-started-automation-scripting/). N-able's API FAQ says scripts must already be in its repository and cannot be passed directly through the API (https://documentation.n-able.com/N-central/preview/rest_api_preview/Content/REST_APIs/api-faq.htm). These API limits may make a genuinely self-serve write-back converter harder than an audit-and-guidance product.
defensible_asset: Potential data moat: a versioned, field-tested library mapping VSA 9 objects and behaviors to target RMM concepts, with recorded validation results and known exceptions. That asset is not evidenced as built today. The migration is deadline-driven and likely a one-time customer project, so switching costs and network effects appear weak unless the mappings become useful for ongoing RMM portability. VSA exports and policies span different object types and assignments, supporting the need for detailed mapping work (https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007940918-What-can-I-migrate-from-On-Premise-to-SaaS-or-SaaS-to-On-Premise; https://help.vsa9.kaseya.com/help/Content/Modules/policy-management/8142.htm).
build_effort: High. A credible product needs a VSA XML/API importer, a normalized representation, vendor-specific translation, dry-run audit output, validation fixtures, and safe handling of credentials and customer configuration. VSA policies include monitoring, alerts, patch management, and procedures (https://help.vsa9.kaseya.com/help/Content/VSA/11519.htm); target behavior and available APIs differ, and NinjaOne documents its script import workflow through the UI (https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/endpoint-management/scripting-and-automation/getting-started-automation-scripting/). An audit-only MVP is materially more feasible than unattended conversion and deployment.
channel: Use inbound SEO for VSA 9 end-of-life and migration queries, opt-in marketplace or integration listings, and contextual paid search where lawful in each target country. Do not use cold email, SMS, DMs, or calls. For UK advertising, the ICO says storage/access technologies used for online advertising require consent; keep non-essential tracking off without consent and check local requirements before advertising in each market (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-the-rules-apply-to-online-advertising/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. A mature audit-and-export SaaS could plausibly fit within 5 hours/week if onboarding, billing, report generation, and routine support are automated; migration edge cases, API changes, and security incidents could exceed that. This is an operating hypothesis, not demonstrated evidence.
automation_reason: Estimated 60% for a mature, narrow audit-and-export service: agents can handle intake, parsing, mapping suggestions, report generation, billing, and common support questions. Human review remains important for conversion exceptions and risky writes. This estimate is not proven by an operating product; VSA and target APIs expose some relevant data and operations, but documented target import limits constrain end-to-end automation (https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007940918-What-can-I-migrate-from-On-Premise-to-SaaS-or-SaaS-to-On-Premise; https://app.ninjaone.com/apidocs-beta/core-resources/operations/createPolicy; https://documentation.n-able.com/N-central/preview/rest_api_preview/Content/REST_APIs/api-faq.htm).
moat_assessment: The moat is prospective, not established. A maintained, validated mapping database could meet the data-moat requirement, but no compiled dataset or field-tested conversion behavior is evidenced. Start with an audit report and mapping suggestions; prove repeatable accuracy and willingness to pay before relying on the moat claim.
desk_test: Within one day and before building, use Google Keyword Planner to check exact-match searches and bid ranges for VSA 9 migration, Kaseya VSA alternatives, and VSA-to-NinjaOne/N-able migration, segmented by US, UK, and relevant European markets. Record the location and date settings; Google defines average monthly searches by those settings (https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6325025?hl=en-en; https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/3022575?hl=en-2). This is a cheap demand screen, not proof of paid intent; the VSA 9 audience size remains unverified.
red_flags: No verified revenue, customer count specific to VSA 9, independent migration price, or paid conversion evidence. Kaseya's end-of-life notice presents only its own migration destinations, while ProVal's recent solution supports Datto (https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb/articles/49926799653265-VSA-9-End-of-Life-Notice; https://content.provaltech.com/docs/38446fc5-ce0a-4319-9471-ce7e327d8a8d/). ProVal's instructions require a VSA token with read/write scope and Datto administrator API rights, illustrating the trust and security burden of migration tooling (https://content.provaltech.com/docs/38446fc5-ce0a-4319-9471-ce7e327d8a8d/). The <=5 owner hours/week and >=50% automation constraints are plausible only as unverified mature-state estimates.
